segments: 256. Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Now the Turks who were inside wrote a letter in Greek by the mouth of the Christians of Neocaesarea, saying to the Greeks:
"Do not trust the Dāwānis {OCR? / governor?} who brought you,
because his letters never cease [coming] from the Turk (Turks?) who is (are) inside,
and he desires to deliver you treacherously to his kinsmen."
And for this reason, panic fell upon the Greeks,
and they set out from Neocaesarea.
And the Turks pursued after them,
and they killed the nephew (sister's son) of the king.
Now when the king heard that his nephew was killed, he gathered a large army,
and went out to the border of the Turks.
And he left the wagons that carried their baggage and their provisions,
and the Greeks entered, taking booty and burning the villages of the Turks—those which had already been emptied of food and of people.
Now the Turks, especially {OCR: mālyesṭā?} the foot soldiers among them, went through the midst of the mountains and the deep ravines of the borderland,
and they reached the large camp of the baggage of the Greeks, and plundered it,
and burned the wagons.
And from here the hope of the Greeks was cut off,
and the Turks grew emboldened against them.
And from the tops of the mountains they rolled boulders down upon the Greeks,
and crushed men and horses.
Then at night the king sent an envoy to the Sultan,
and sought peace.
And because he too was placed in fear,
he immediately agreed.
And he assigned three Turkish emirs,
and they went in attendance upon the king until they entered within his borders.
And because in the camp of the Greeks which had been plundered,
there were many churches and crosses and ornaments,
and also the cross which had in it a piece of the wood of the Crucifixion was stripped away (taken),
the king sent much gold to the Sultan,
and took back the cross.
And in this year died Najm al-Dīn, the lord of Mardin,
he who during the twenty-two years that he reigned,
the Christians and churches and monasteries were in great prosperity with him.
And after him his son Quṭb al-Dīn reigned,
and he engaged in warfare with his uncles, the lord of Khānī and the lord of Dārā.
And afterwards he made peace with them,
and they came to him,
and were in his subjugation.
And a rumor went out about him that he had died,
and the Ma'addite Arabs began raiding in his territory.
When he recovered,
he killed thousands of the Arabs,
